visits.text: Carved into the rock of the Bock from 1644 onwards, the Bock Casemates form an underground network that earned Luxembourg the nickname 'Gibraltar of the North'. These defensive galleries, enlarged by Vauban then the Austrians, once stretched for 23 km. UNESCO-listed since 1994, they offer plunging views over the Grund through their loopholes. Narrow staircases: avoid with large luggage.

Some call it Europe's finest balcony, and the Chemin de la Corniche almost deserves the title. This path laid out on the old ramparts overlooks the Alzette valley and the Grund quarter. The promenade is short, free, and accessible on foot from the old town. Best light in late afternoon.

Notre-Dame Cathedral of Luxembourg blends late Gothic and Renaissance touches, a stone's throw from Place de la Constitution. Its crypt houses the tombs of the grand ducal family. Beside it stands the Gëlle Fra, the 'golden lady', a war memorial perched on its column. Cathedral entry is free.

activities.text: Descend to the Grund quarter, down below, via the free panoramic Pfaffenthal lift or on foot. Below, the Alzette winds between old houses and the former Neumünster Abbey, now a cultural venue. Public transport is free throughout the country—make the most of it. The contrast between upper and lower town is striking.
